_comment: What foundry_pull.py fetches, and how it is tagged. Folder roots are pulled whole (General/<bucket>/<Character>/<tier actors>); listed actors are pulled individually and grouped under the named character.

roots._why: work-in-progress characters; badged as drafts on the roster

actors.note: the 100 XP actor with the completed twenty questions; the other Shinjō Harunobu actor (FCqx2vUqaoQHEK5w) has none

campaigns._comment: campaign tag by character slug; anything not listed has no campaign

corrections._comment: field fixes applied on extract; the Foundry record has the typo

nasu-kogo._why: Foundry records 'Shoshuro Shadoweaver School'; the compendium roll spells it 'Shosuro Shadowweaver School'

tonbo-asahi.identity.school: Dragonfly Grace of the Spirits School
tonbo-asahi._why: Foundry records 'Dragonfly Grace of the Spirits'; the compendium roll has ' School'

iuchi-temur._why: actor records 'Iuchi Meishōdō Master'; the roll has ' School' on the end

portraits._comment: portrait path per slug, relative to the repo root

_derive_tiers_comment: characters Foundry holds at one point only; scripts/derive_tiers.py rebuilds their earlier XP tiers

promoted._comment: slugs promoted out of draft. The Draft folder and the Creator both mark characters as drafts; promotion is the deliberate act of saying one is finished, and is recorded here so a re-extract cannot silently undo it. Use scripts/promote.py.

title_aliases._comment: campaign-renamed titles -> the compendium title whose curriculum they use. The character keeps its own name; only the curriculum lookup is redirected.

Personal Advisor to Miya Misato._why: an Advisor title (Emerald Empire p.249) with a campaign-specific name. Corroborated by cost: the character's title records xp_cost 36, which is the Advisor title's cost.

ai_proxy._comment: deployed URL of worker/ — the Anthropic shim the published Creator calls. Empty until deployed; the Creator then asks for a pasted key instead.

concepts._comment: Loose concept material for a draft, written by the author. It is authoring context only: the Creator feeds it to every AI suggestion and never exports it, so it shapes a character without becoming part of one. Kept here rather than in src/characters/<slug>.json so a --force re-extract cannot lose it, and so it stays out of the promoted record.
concepts.isawa-chisato:
Isawa Chisato is a devout shugenja of the Phoenix Clan, serving the Elemental Master of Fire with the duty to defend the purity of the Tao. She believes that fire burns away falsehoods, and she has been tasked with destroying heretical teachings and ensuring spiritual doctrine remains pure. Though she seeks understanding, she is often impatient with those who do not see the truth as clearly as she does.

Her confidence is unshakable — she speaks passionately and forcefully, never softening her convictions. Yet, despite her outward certainty, she secretly suppresses her own doubt, fearing that her teachings could be flawed. She holds her parents on a pedestal, believing they set her on the right path, though she has never truly questioned their guidance.

Chisato finds peace in tending sacred flames, seeing fire as both a destroyer and an illuminator of truth. Her greatest accomplishment was purifying a tainted shrine, proving her faith in divine order. However, her harsh judgment of others and fear of being ignored sometimes alienate those who might otherwise listen, making her mission both righteous and isolating.
concepts.doji-sayaka:
Doji Sayaka is a refined diplomat serving the Doji daimyō, tasked with monitoring the Perfect Land Sect to ensure the Crane are not caught off guard. If necessary, she is expected to subtly undermine its leadership and cause its collapse. A master of diplomacy, she always speaks in extended metaphors, guiding conversations with elegance and intent.

She is impeccably dressed, maintaining an air of poise and control. She appears perfectly at ease with any outcome, rarely showing joy or displeasure, always maintaining a neutral mask. Despite this, she secretly struggles with sincerity, as her life has been one of perceptions and careful maneuvering, making true honesty difficult.

Sayaka occasionally disguises herself as a peasant, blending among the common folk to see the world from their eyes. Though she longs for genuine connection, she keeps others at a careful distance, fearing vulnerability. Deep down, she sees death as the final performance, believing that even in her last moments, she must meet her fate with grace and dignity.
concepts.iuchi-temur:
Iuchi Temur is a Unicorn shugenja and healer, sent to aid the Dragon Clan while ensuring that any affliction affecting them does not spread to his own people. His duty is to uncover the nature of the threat before it spreads, balancing his compassionate instincts with the need to protect the Unicorn. Though he follows Bushidō, he prioritizes kindness over rigid duty, believing that a healer's first obligation is to those in need.

Temur wears furs, his beard carefully braided, and his hair in a bun, presenting himself as rugged yet composed. He carries himself with calm reassurance, making others feel safe and cared for. Despite this, he suppresses his homesickness, longing to return to the one he loves, while fearing that his duty may cost him his own happiness.

He finds peace in caring for his steed and compounding medicines, yet he struggles to take care of his own needs, constantly prioritizing others before himself. Though he once contained a deadly outbreak, proving his worth as a healer, he fears the corruption of the Shadowlands most of all, knowing that even magic has its limits.
concepts.jinrai:
Jinrai is a former ashigaru turned monk, now a wandering teacher of the Perfect Land Sect. He believes that all people are equal in the eyes of enlightenment, rejecting the Celestial Order and spreading the sect's teachings to the common folk. Though he preaches peace, he struggles to let go of his resentment toward the samurai, finding it difficult to forgive their oppression.

His presence radiates determination and purpose, and he speaks passionately and inspiringly, ensuring that his words move those who listen. However, he suppresses hope, fearing that his efforts will ultimately change nothing. Though he enjoys luxuries when offered, he tries to live simply, though he sometimes indulges in a warm bed or fine meal.

Jinrai once converted a violent bandit to the Perfect Land Sect, proving the power of faith over force. He finds peace in chanting sutras, yet he secretly longs to be free of responsibility, growing weary of carrying the burden of leadership. His view of mortality is simple — his life is a sacrifice worth making if it furthers the cause of enlightenment.
concepts.kurosawa-genzo:
Kurosawa Genzō is a deserter-turned-rōnin duelist, wandering the land and offering his sword to whoever can meet his price. Though he carries himself with the discipline of a samurai, he no longer claims the title, instead forging his own sense of honor. He avoids pointless fights, only drawing his blade when there is purpose behind it.

His scarred, battle-hardened face still carries boyish charm, though he maintains a gruff default demeanor to keep others at a distance. He struggles to trust others, fearing betrayal or obligation, and regrets abandoning his duty, wondering if he can ever reclaim his lost honor. He sharpens his blade to find peace, a steady ritual that reminds him that he is still in control of his fate.

Genzō once spared a defeated opponent who later repaid the debt, reinforcing his belief that honor is found in action, not station. However, he knows that one wrong move could lead to an ignominious death, a fate he refuses to accept. Though he gambles on fights, he does not gamble with his own survival — he has lived this long, and he does not intend to die easily.
concepts.kitsuki-nagiko:
Kitsuki Nagiko — she/her — Emerald Magistrate

**Kitsuki Investigator** · Dragon · Courtier/Bushi · Air +1, Earth +1 · Honor 45 · she/her
**Emerald Magistrate**

### Cards
- **The Emperor, reversed** — rigid; will follow her method thoroughly regardless of what anyone else thinks.
- **Knight of Swords, reversed** — tactless, unsympathetic; idealises a moment when people would simply cede to her correct, factual assessments.
- **Knight of Pentacles, upright** — hard-working, practical, uncomplaining about her own difficulties. She will complain about others.

### Reading
Two Knights and a reversed Emperor. She holds the *office* of authority while both other cards say she is still a Knight — in service, in motion, not yet a master. She has the writ before she has the maturity, and the Emperor reversed is what fills that gap with procedure.

The two Knights run at opposite tempos, and that is her: patient with the work, impatient with people. Nine hours on a body, ninety seconds on your feelings about it.

The Knight of Pentacles gives her a running audit of who is falling short, while she says nothing about her own difficulties. That isn't hypocrisy she is aware of — it doesn't occur to her that the two are the same ledger.

The Knight of Swords fantasy is her emotional core: a room where facts land and everyone concedes. Rokugan is not that room, and the Kitsuki evidence method specifically has contested standing outside Dragon lands. The Emperor reversed therefore puts her in the position of insisting on a procedure that the people present may not be obliged to accept.

### Established
- Knows Sanpei owes money. Does **not** know his lenders are criminal or local.

### Candidate hooks (unpicked)
- **Adversity:** Bluntness (Air) · Bullheaded (Earth)
- **Anxiety:** Perfectionism · Impatience · Obtuse
- **Distinction:** Famously Reliable (Earth) · Legal Scholarship (Air)
- **Passion:** Honest Work (Earth)
- **Title:** Emerald Magistrate

### Open
- What does she carry without complaining?
- Career stage — early/proving, mid/unpromoted, or experienced but resented?
- Is she the sole Emerald Magistrate?

---

### Cross-character

**Nagiko ↔ Chiyo** — Nagiko is tactless by construction; Chiyo is triggered by condescension. Two characters who abrade without either being written toward it.
**Nagiko ↔ Nergüi** — Both drew Knight of Pentacles. The bond is completion, not warmth. Nagiko's contempt for everyone is precisely why Nergüi is treated as an equal.
**Nagiko ↔ Ryōsei** — Both unbreakable, by incompatible mechanisms: rigidity versus balance. This will show the first time they disagree about how to run the investigation.
concepts.kuni-ryosei:
Kuni Ryōsei — she/her — Yoriki

**Kuni Purifier** · Crab · Shugenja/Bushi · Earth +1, Fire +1 · Honor 35 · she/her
**Yoriki**

### Cards
- **King of Cups** — a willingness to explore the dark side, but never in a way that has risked or tempted her.
- **Queen of Wands, reversed** — there is a pull towards darkness, and she knows the path to take.
- **Temperance (XIV)** — this is avoided because she maintains a life balanced in all things, not overly rigid.

### Reading
The calmest spread in the party, and the only adult one — King, Queen, and a major, where others drew Pages and Knights. She is not developing; she is maintained. That is a function, not a flaw.

King of Cups is competence, not innocence. She has looked at the thing directly, professionally, repeatedly, and it never got a hook in. The exposure is the job. What the card says is that the exposure never converted into appetite.

The Queen of Wands reversed matters because of the precision of the phrasing — not vague temptation, but *she knows the path to take*. Which is simply true of her training. Understanding how mahō works is the curriculum. Nothing needs to be discovered; something would only need to be decided.

Temperance is a practice, not a victory. Not-rigid was specified, and it matters: this holds because it is maintained daily, not because it is locked. The opposite mechanism from Nagiko, who also does not fall but stays upright by being immovable.

### Established
- **The pull is toward developing weaponry that can combat the darkness, or those turned by it.**
- Maintained by a **daily discipline**.
- **One other person** knows how completely she understands that path.

### On the pull
It isn't toward darkness. It's toward a workshop. She doesn't want power or forbidden knowledge — she wants a thing that *works*. That is the most dangerous shape a temptation can take, because it never presents as temptation. It presents as work. A better weapon is not a moral compromise. Neither is the second. It's the eleventh, built from what the tenth taught her, using the only material that reliably answers.

It is also the logical endpoint of her clan's own doctrine rather than a deviation from it. Crab pragmatism says do what works against the Shadowlands. She has followed that further than the people who say it aloud.

The daily discipline now makes structural sense: you don't guard against a to-do list with a vow. A vow is for a memory; a daily practice is for something that regenerates every morning.

**In this adventure:** the party will find the cult's apparatus. For six of them it's evidence. For her it's material. Nobody has to tempt her and the cult never has to notice she exists — the pressure arrives the moment she's in the room, and it arrives as curiosity about workmanship.

### Candidate hooks (unpicked)
- **Distinction:** Famously Neutral (Earth) · Syncretic Philosophy (Water)
- **Passion:** Armament (Earth) · Tea (Void) · Religious Study (Void)
- **Title:** Witch Hunter
- *Steer off* Reformed Mahō-Tsukai — the King of Cups says study, never practice.

### Open
- What is the daily discipline?
- Who is the one other person?
- Has she already built anything?

---

### Cross-character

**Nagiko ↔ Ryōsei** — Both unbreakable, by incompatible mechanisms: rigidity versus balance. This will show the first time they disagree about how to run the investigation.
**Ryōsei ↔ Nergüi** — The party's two supernatural specialists. He reads; she builds. Different verbs entirely.
concepts.iuchi-nergui:
Iuchi Nergüi — he/him — Yoriki to Nagiko

**Ujik Diviner** · Iuchi family, Ujik background · Sage · Void +1, Water +1 · Honor 40 · he/him
**Yoriki to Nagiko**

Name meaning: "no one" — traditionally given to a child to hide them from malicious spirits. Every Rokugani who asks his name is told *no one*, and has to decide whether that's insolence, a joke, or a foreigner mangling the language. The Hermit reversed generates itself in any scene, unstaged.

### Cards
- **The Chariot** — goal-oriented, balanced, driven.
- **Knight of Pentacles** — wants to see a mission through to the end; is not generally in control of it; currently serving the Kitsuki as yoriki.
- **The Hermit, reversed** — his Rokugani is imperfect; he stands out and is somewhat ostracised. The Kitsuki doesn't treat him any differently, however — she's an asshole to everyone.

### Reading
The Chariot's image is a driver holding two opposing forces in harness. Here he is *in* the harness rather than holding it. All that drive, pointed down a road someone else chose — the specific frustration of a competent subordinate.

Knight of Pentacles is the second appearance of that card in this party. Nagiko drew it upright too, and it means the same thing both times: finish the work. That is the actual bond between them, and there is nothing warm in it. They aren't loyal to each other, they're loyal to completion, and that turns out to be enough.

The Hermit upright is the seeker who withdraws for wisdom and returns carrying a lamp — a diviner's job description. Reversed, the apartness isn't chosen and the lamp buys him nothing. The role that should earn deference earns distance, and the reason is accent, not competence.

Nagiko's tactlessness is a liability in every other scene she's in. Here it is the one place he is treated as an equal, because she is contemptuous of everyone equally. An ugly, real basis for trust.

### Candidate hooks (unpicked)
- **Adversity:** Gaijin Name, Culture, or Appearance (Fire) — the Hermit reversed nearly verbatim
- **Anxiety:** Loneliness (Void) · Isolation (Earth)
- **Distinction:** Indomitable Will (Earth) · Sixth Sense (Void) · Affinity with (Void)
- **Passion:** Fortune-Telling (Void)
- **Title:** Yoriki

### Open
- What is the Chariot driving toward?
- How did he come to serve Nagiko?
- Where does the imperfect Rokugani show most — accent, literacy, or idiom?

---

### Cross-character

**Nagiko ↔ Nergüi** — Both drew Knight of Pentacles. The bond is completion, not warmth. Nagiko's contempt for everyone is precisely why Nergüi is treated as an equal.
**Ryōsei ↔ Nergüi** — The party's two supernatural specialists. He reads; she builds. Different verbs entirely.
concepts.shosuro-hisano:
Shosuro Hisano — they/them — Scorpion asset on loan to Nagiko

**Shosuro Infiltrator** · Scorpion · Shinobi/Courtier · Air +1, Fire +1 · Honor 30 · they/them
**Not a yoriki.** A long-dormant Scorpion asset whose use has been granted to Nagiko as a favour from the Scorpion.

### Cards
- **Six of Wands** — a highly regarded performer.
- **Eight of Pentacles, reversed** — wants to be able to manage other artists, but is too embroiled in their own craft.
- **Page of Wands** — also blocked by inexperience, but has big ideas for what they hope to do as they move into more of a producer role.

### Reading
Nothing in this spread is about espionage. Three cards on craft and ambition, none on tradecraft. Hisano is an artist who happens to have been trained to lie professionally, rather than a spy with a cover story.

The acclaim was accumulated *during the sleep*. A dormant asset lives their cover, and theirs is a stage career they've had nothing to do but excel at. The cover stopped being a cover and became the only life they've actually lived.

Six of Wands over Page of Wands is an unusual position: senior at the thing they want to stop doing, novice at the thing they want to start. Both true simultaneously. Not impostor syndrome — a person whose actual credential is in the wrong field, and who knows it.

The Eight of Pentacles reversed is the mechanism. Excellence keeps them at the bench. Every strong performance earns another performance. Success is the cage, and it's invisible from outside, because it looks like a career going well.

The Page of Wands does double duty: inexperienced as a producer, and rusty as an operative. The one thing everyone will assume they're good at is the thing they're least current in.

### Established
- They have always known they were a sleeper — it had been filed away in the background for years, and had stopped feeling live.
- When the Scorpion called it in it landed as **unwelcome and as a possible way out of the rut, simultaneously**. Both are true; neither cancels the other, and they couldn't tell you which is truer.
- The Scorpion **know** they want out of performing.

### The craft (my pick, at your request)
**Masked stage drama**, acclaimed for a *single signature role* played for years.

It carries all three cards at once: the acclaim is real and specific; the role is the cage, because you cannot step behind the curtain to run a troupe while you are the reason people bought tickets; and the producer ambition has concrete shape — stage new work with other actors instead of the same play until they die.

The Scorpion irony is free: a clan mask by custom, a second mask by profession, and underneath both someone who has been asleep long enough to be unsure which face is load-bearing.

*Runner-up: puppetry — a performer who already directs figures, making the producer ambition feel like scale rather than a leap.*

### Structural note
They are the odd one out. Everyone else is bound by duty to the investigation. Hisano is borrowed property whose obligation runs back to Scorpion lands. They can be recalled mid-case, and the person who recalls them isn't at the table.

### Candidate hooks (unpicked)
- **Distinction:** Famously Successful (Fire)
- **Adversity:** Overconfidence in Creativity (Fire) · Encompassing Duty (Earth)
- **Anxiety:** Fear of Stagnation (Earth) · Fear of Mediocrity (Fire)
- **Passion:** Kabuki (Air) · Attention (Fire)

### Open
- How much does Nagiko know about what she's been loaned — the full terms, that they're Scorpion-loaned but not what they are, or does she think they're an ordinary yoriki?

---
concepts.kasuga-chiyo:
Kasuga Chiyo — she/her — Governor Mugatsu's assigned minder

**Kasuga Smuggler** · Tortoise · Courtier · Air +1, Water +1 · Honor 29 · she/her
**Not a yoriki.** Assigned by Governor Kasuga Mugatsu as the magistrates' "guide."

### Cards
- **King of Swords, reversed** — she is acting out; she has made bad investments; she is easily provoked.
- **Nine of Swords** — she does not see any future for herself; she feels doomed.
- **The Fool** — she is deluding herself that this mission, that helping out this Emerald Magistrate, is a kind of fresh start.

### Reading
Her standing came from her judgement, and her judgement failed. She is privately certain she's finished, and she is misreading a leash as an open road.

A partnership leaves paper. A lost cargo is deniable; a partnership is a thing two people entered into, and someone somewhere has a record. Her exposure is *discoverable* — the Kitsuki can find her without her confessing. Her ruin and the party's investigation are the same document.

Because she's centrally implicated, the Nine of Swords is **accurate** rather than distorted dread. She has correctly assessed her position. She can't be talked down.

Condescension is the one trigger she can't avoid: Emerald Magistrates condescending to a Tortoise smuggler is the default state of the assignment, not a scene anyone has to write. So her King of Swords temper gets reached repeatedly, for free.

**She has no idea what the partnership actually is.** That reverses the obvious reading and improves her. The dread isn't about the cult — it's about ordinary ruin: the partnership, the money, the standing. She is correct that she's finished and wrong about why. The Fool sharpens accordingly: she isn't hiding evidence, she's *carrying* it into the magistrate's presence and calling it a fresh start. She can still be surprised by what the party finds, which makes her playable rather than static.

### Established
- Her ruin is **central** — she is implicated in the adventure's plot.
- The bad investment took the shape of **a partnership she entered**.
- **Being condescended to** gets her temper up fastest.
- **She has no idea** what the partnership actually is.

### Candidate hooks (unpicked)
- **Adversity:** Debt to (Water) · Unsavory Past (Water)
- **Distinction:** Criminal Connections (Air) · Well Connected in {City} (Water)
- **Passion:** Travel (Water) — the Fool's card
- **Bushidō:** Sincerity is the tenet she's furthest from and wants most
- *Dark Secret is now retired* — she has no secret, she has a blind spot.

### Open
- Who was the partner? Will the party encounter them, are they dead, or gone?
- Who else currently knows she's implicated?

---

### Cross-character

**Nagiko ↔ Chiyo** — Nagiko is tactless by construction; Chiyo is triggered by condescension. Two characters who abrade without either being written toward it.
**Chiyo ↔ Sanpei** — Two debts, both structurally unsolvable, opposite outlooks. Her Nine of Swords says she knows hers is terminal; his whole spread says he still believes his is fixable. One of them is right.
**Chiyo ↔ Ichirō** — Employer and muscle, both in the dark. She hired protection while believing she has no future; either she fears something specific she hasn't named, or the Fool's delusion ran far enough that she started behaving like a person with prospects.
**Two criminal threads into the port's underworld** — Chiyo's (retrospective, already implicated) and Sanpei's (prospective, about to be leveraged). Two independent doors, one doomed and one desperate. Worth noting the criminal layer of Slow Tide Harbor is load-bearing for two of seven.
concepts.ichiro-tsutomu:
Ichirō Tsutomu — he/him — Chiyo's hired muscle

**Ichirō Grappler** · Badger · Bushi · Earth +1, Water +1 · Honor 45 · he/him
**Not a yoriki.** Hired by Chiyo personally as her own muscle.

### Cards
- **Two of Wands, reversed** — risk averse, defensive.
- **Ten of Swords, reversed** — came out of failure pivoting into something else, or with the gumption to re-enter the sport.
- **Justice (XI)** — he got absolutely trounced because of his cautious style.

### Reading
Justice is cruel in a specific way: no bad call, no injury, no rigged bout. He lost because of how he fights, and the verdict was correct. An unfair defeat lets a man stay who he is and blame the world; a just one doesn't. And the Two of Wands reversed says the thing he'd have to change is temperamental, not tactical. You don't decide to stop being risk-averse.

The defensive grappler picture is concrete: waiting, not committing, letting the other man make the mistake. Against an opponent who doesn't make mistakes, that's standing there while it happens.

**His liability in sport is an asset in law enforcement.** A magistrate's retinue needs suspects alive and witnesses unbroken. The strongest body in the party being the least inclined to commit to violence is precisely right for a portside interrogation. Whether he's realised that is a better arc than "learns to be aggressive."

He is also the only one whose failure is public. Chiyo's ruin is secret, Sanpei's debt hidden, Hisano's rut looks like success, Nergüi's difference is visible but isn't shame. Ichirō lost in front of a crowd — nobody can threaten to expose a man whose worst moment already had an audience.

**The pivot isn't upward.** Several months out from losing a title he was favoured for, and the work he's found is being someone's available muscle in a portside town. Not a new calling — the same asset, his body, rented out in a worse setting.

**"Favoured for" is the sharpest detail.** He never held it. The room expected him to take it and his caution let it go. There's no title to reclaim, only one to finally earn, and the version of himself who could earn it is the version he isn't.

**The one decisive act of his life was leaving.** He didn't drift — he came looking for work. A man who lost a title by never committing made exactly one commitment: get out and sell the only thing that still works.

### Established
- Defeat was **several months ago**.
- It cost him **a title he was favoured for** (never held).
- He **came to the port looking for work specifically**.
- He knows **nothing** about Chiyo's situation.

### Structural note
He's the party's blind spot by construction: he answers to Chiyo, Chiyo is centrally implicated, and he knows nothing. He isn't cheap to turn because he'd take money — he's cheap to turn because someone only has to tell him the truth about his employer, and that costs nothing.

### Candidate hooks (unpicked)
- **Anxiety:** Meekness (Fire) — his weak ring governing aggression
- **Adversity:** Whispers of Failure (Fire)
- **Distinction:** Keen Balance (Earth) · Indomitable Will (Earth)
- **Title:** Sumai Master — useful as the thing he doesn't have

*Essentially settled.*

---
concepts.sanpei:
Sanpei — he/him — Hired by Nagiko; formal status undefined

**The Wandering Blade** · Rōnin · Bushi · Earth +1 + choice · Honor 35 · he/him
**Status undefined.** Hired by Nagiko; not a yoriki.

### Cards
- **Three of Pentacles** — promising, and has been granted this opportunity to serve an Emerald Magistrate; determined not to fuck it up.
- **Queen of Pentacles** — he just wants a lord to serve, material guarantees, etc.
- **Ten of Pentacles, reversed** — any such lord would have to pay off the many debts that threaten to catch up with him, many of them unsavoury.

### Reading
Every card is Pentacles. No swords, no wands, no cups — nothing about honour, glory, the blade, or the spirit. For a rōnin in Rokugan that's pointed: his entire inner life is material security, in a culture that considers material security beneath mention.

The Ten of Pentacles is the inheritance card, drawn upside down. A rōnin's condition is the absence of that card. Reversed, it's worse than absent — where a legacy should be, there's a negative balance. He didn't inherit nothing; he inherited a bill.

His problem is arithmetic, not sentiment. He isn't trying to impress anyone; he's trying to be worth more than he costs, because any lord who takes him on assumes a liability and he knows it. The Three of Pentacles reads as *don't let anyone see why I might fuck this up* rather than as ambition.

The Queen of Pentacles is refreshingly unromantic. Not a name restored, not vengeance, not enlightenment. A roof, a stipend, a lord, regular meals.

**Protection money isn't a sum, it's a subscription.** You don't clear it; you keep paying until the lender stops existing. So the Queen of Pentacles want may not be purchasable — a lord could cover a debt, but covering a tribute means buying out the lender or removing them, and neither is a thing you ask a new patron for. His plan may have no version that works.

**"His own" removes his excuse.** No inherited bill, no debt assumed for a friend. He built this. The Three of Pentacles promise runs against his own documented judgement, and the Queen of Pentacles isn't really a want for a lord — it's a want to be saved from himself by someone with more money.

**His value to his creditors just went up.** He walked into their town, behind on payments, wearing a magistrate's authority. Yesterday he was a debtor worth what he could be beaten for; today he's a man inside an Emerald Magistrate's investigation who owes them money. They don't want him dead — they want him useful.

**Nagiko has miscategorised it.** She knows he owes money, which in her framework is a personal failing to be noted. She doesn't know the lenders are criminal or local. She filed it and moved on — exactly what the Emperor reversed does with information that doesn't fit the method. The clock is therefore driven by the creditors, not by her discovery. They'll reach him long before she reaches the truth.

Useful for you: this is a compromise vector with nothing supernatural in it. It runs parallel to the cult and needs no connection to it.

### Established
- The debts are **his own**.
- Owed to **protection money / criminal lenders**.
- Nagiko knows **only that he owes money**.
- He is **behind** on payments.
- His creditors **operate in Slow Tide Harbor**.

### Candidate hooks (unpicked)
- **Adversity:** Debt to (Water) · Pursued by (Water)
- **Anxiety/Adversity:** Whispers of Poverty (Water)
- **Distinction:** Scrounger (Water) · Seasoned (Void)
- **Passion:** Hot Pot (Earth) — exactly what a Queen of Pentacles wants, and costs nothing to want
- **Title:** *In Service to a Lord* — worth noting as the thing he does **not** have and is playing for

### Open
- **What is his formal status?** Personal retainer, hired sword, provisional-with-a-view-to-permanent?
- Does he know his creditors operate here?
- Do the creditors see the posting as a problem or a prize?

---

### Cross-character

**Chiyo ↔ Sanpei** — Two debts, both structurally unsolvable, opposite outlooks. Her Nine of Swords says she knows hers is terminal; his whole spread says he still believes his is fixable. One of them is right.
**Sanpei ↔ Ichirō** — Two bodies for hire, same want, opposite approaches: one auditioning for permanence and terrified of losing the chance, one taking wages and never asking for more.
**Two criminal threads into the port's underworld** — Chiyo's (retrospective, already implicated) and Sanpei's (prospective, about to be leveraged). Two independent doors, one doomed and one desperate. Worth noting the criminal layer of Slow Tide Harbor is load-bearing for two of seven.

dsl_text_exceptions._comment: Catalog entries referenced by a character whose rules text cannot come from the DSL corpus. Each needs a stated reason; scripts/dsl_rules_text.py fails on any that is not listed here. A key of the form 'sub_type:<name>' excepts a whole class where the corpus has no prose by design. A reason beginning DEFERRED is a gap Jordan has seen and chosen to leave for now — it is still counted and named on every run, never folded into the settled exclusions. Entries listed here keep Foundry's text and are marked text_source=foundry in the built data. An entry stops being needed once the corpus carries it, and a stale one is worth removing rather than leaving: five went on 2026-09-02 — Calligraphy Set, Finger of Jade, Personal Seal or Chop and Poison (One Vial), four of the six personal effects deferred on 2026-08-30, plus Kubi Bukuro, which had been listed as flavour-only. Quiver of Arrow and Traveling pack are the two personal effects still outstanding.
dsl_text_exceptions.Journal of observations: No text in Foundry either — nothing is lost by dropping it.
dsl_text_exceptions.Naga Armor: Authored in the l5r5e-compendia-sortilege module, not in a printed book (source_book null, page 0), so it has no corpus counterpart by construction. No text in Foundry either — nothing is lost by dropping it.
dsl_text_exceptions.Personal Pearl (Sacred): Authored in the l5r5e-compendia-sortilege module, not in a printed book (source_book null, page 0), so it has no corpus counterpart by construction. No text in Foundry either — nothing is lost by dropping it.
dsl_text_exceptions.Quiver of Arrow: DEFERRED (Jordan, 2026-08-30) — real mechanical text the corpus does not carry: a Core Rulebook personal effect. Converting it into titterpig-dsl-l5r5e is the fix, and Jordan has decided not to do that yet, so it keeps Foundry's text meanwhile. Deferred by decision, not overlooked.
dsl_text_exceptions.Scroll satchel: No text in Foundry either — nothing is lost by dropping it.
dsl_text_exceptions.Traveling pack: DEFERRED (Jordan, 2026-08-30) — real mechanical text the corpus does not carry: a Core Rulebook personal effect. Converting it into titterpig-dsl-l5r5e is the fix, and Jordan has decided not to do that yet, so it keeps Foundry's text meanwhile. Deferred by decision, not overlooked.
dsl_text_exceptions.sub_type:weapon: The corpus states a weapon's rules as its stat line (category, skill, range, damage, deadliness, grips, qualities, rarity, price), which the sheet renders in its own columns. Foundry's description is flavour prose with no rules content, so no weapon has corpus prose and none is missing any. Stated for the whole sub_type rather than name by name, so adding a character who carries a different weapon does not trip the gate.

school_corpus_aliases._comment: Compendium school name -> the DSL corpus's spelling, for scripts/generate_pregen.py. The reverse of school_aliases above: that one fixes a character whose school name differs from the compendium, this one bridges the compendium to the corpus.

school_name_corrections._comment: The Foundry l5r5e system's core-journal-school-curriculum pack misspells two school titles, and l5r5e-compendia-sortilege mirrors it. Corrected at catalog load in scripts/build.py, so the site shows what the book prints and the compendium title never reaches a page. Verified against the source text in ~/Working/sources/l5r5e. Delete an entry once the upstream pack is fixed.
